title: Deep Readonly State Container with Lens-Based Immutability
businessContext: In a high-frequency trading and portfolio management dashboard, unintended in-place mutations of deeply nested asset objects caused subtle desynchronizations between the UI chart and underlying websocket order feeds.
problemStatement: Create a recursive utility type `DeepReadonly<T>` that converts all nested objects, arrays, and maps into immutable types at compile time. Then create a safe updater function `updateAtPath(state, path, updater)` that enforces type safety on nested property updates.
constraints: Must recursively make all nested properties readonly, including arrays and Maps.
Must preserve function types without making their signatures unusable.
Do not use any third-party libraries.
candidateTasks: Write recursive `DeepReadonly<T>` utility type covering primitives, functions, arrays, and plain objects.
Explain why TypeScript readonly is a compile-time check and how it pairs with runtime `Object.freeze`.
hints: Check for function types first so you do not turn functions into empty objects.

testCases.name: Retrieves nested property from deeply immutable state

alternativeApproaches: Using Immer.js with Draft<T> and Immutable<T> library types.
Using Immutable.js Record and Map data structures.
commonMistakes: Applying object mapping to functions, turning methods into {} types.
Forgetting that Array is also an object, mapping it to { [0]: ..., [1]: ... } instead of ReadonlyArray.
